error_reason: The WebSurfer agent repeatedly executed the exact same search query ('Britannica France Roman Gaul 400-500 Crossing of the Rhine' or similar variations) from Turn 8 through Turn 14 without executing a new search, scrolling, or updating the viewport to retrieve the actual content. Despite the Planner indicating a lack of visible information, the WebSurfer failed to adapt its strategy to actually acquire the necessary data, resulting in wasted turns with no progress.

suggested_fix.fix_text: The agent stopped searching for 'Britannica' after Turn 6 and repeatedly searched for the same query variations without actually browsing the result page (scrolling). Instead of blindly searching 'Britannica' repeatedly, the agent should explicitly attempt to open the Britannica result link from the previous turn and scroll down to view the full content, rather than just re-querying the search engine.

probe_details.notes: The proposed error analysis is incorrect because it misidentifies the root cause. The agent did not blindly repeat the exact same string; it iterated with slight variations in query terms ('Crossing of the Rhine 406 Britannica' vs 'Britannica Crossing of the Rhine 406 December 31 Britannica'). The real error was a navigation strategy failure: the agent failed to click/search within the specific result page it found to scroll and read the content, instead getting stuck in a loop of re-submitting search queries to DuckDuckGo. This wasted turns (Turns 8-14) because the agent was never actually viewing the Britannica page content needed to extract the specific date confirmation, leading to the failure state.
